Where it began

Senuran Muthusamy was born in Durban on 22 February 1994. His family's roots lie in South India, with relatives in Nagapattinam, in Tamil Nadu.

His first senior side was KwaZulu-Natal, for whom he played in the Africa T20 Cup in 2015 and again in 2018. Later he moved to North West, and in March 2022, on the very first day of the One-Day Cup, he made his maiden List A hundred: exactly 100 against Western Province, from 106 balls.

The player

Muthusamy bats and bowls, and South Africa wanted both. They picked him for their tour of India in 2019, and he made his Test debut on 2 October that year.

The first wicket of his Test career could hardly have been grander. India's captain, Virat Kohli, was caught and bowled by him for 20. Plenty of bowlers wait a lifetime for a scalp like that. He had it in his first match.

By November 2026 he had played 8 Tests, between 2019 and 2025, scoring 388 runs at 55.43 with a hundred, a best of 109, and two fifties. With the ball he took 23 wickets at 26.35, including two five-wicket hauls and a ten-wicket match, with a best of six for 117. He also held 7 catches.

What made him special

Muthusamy offers a captain two jobs in one player. His batting average is the sort usually kept for specialist batters, and four of his eleven innings ended with him not out, which tells you how hard he was to remove once settled.

His bowling grew into a weapon too. A ten-wicket Test is something many bowlers never manage in a whole career. If there is a gap in his record, it is simply the number of matches: eight Tests is a small sample, and a few more Tests would let the numbers speak even louder.

Away from the middle

He made his one-day international debut in February 2025, in a three-nation series in Pakistan. In January 2026 he agreed to join Kent as their overseas player, for the T20 Blast and eight County Championship matches.

And finally

In 2017 he was picked by the Cape Town Knight Riders for a brand new T20 league. The league was postponed and then cancelled before a ball was bowled. Some players would call that bad luck. Muthusamy might call it practice in patience, which served him well when Test cricket finally came calling.
